description: CANDIDATE-BUILT scripted experiment queue for the CPU stand-in engine. Each entry is a genuine build/config change to tasks/harness-design/standin/Dockerfile rendered into a unified diff by ScriptedProposer. Order matters: kept experiments become the new last-good baseline for later comparisons. Edits with "regex": true match the current (possibly already-patched) build context so the queue does not depend on which earlier experiments were kept.

experiments.hypothesis: Decode is compute-bound on CPU; raising --threads/--threads-batch from 4 to the 8 cores allotted to the container should raise FTGR and lower TTFT.
Control experiment: a single decode thread must regress FTGR and TTFT; the decision rule should revert it.
Benchmark prompts are ~30-40 tokens, so shrinking --batch-size/--ubatch-size from 512 to 64 should not change TTFT or FTGR measurably (expected no_change).
A server-side default --repeat-penalty 1.5 could shorten rambling outputs and finish faster, but it changes greedy argmax; the golden-output gate must reject it (expected gate_failed).
Fault injection: serving on port 8001 while the contract expects 8000 makes the server unreachable; the startup timeout must detect the hung/unreachable server (expected error).
Fault injection: compiling with GGML_AVX512=ON on a host without AVX-512 produces a binary that dies with an illegal instruction at startup; the loop must log it as error and keep last-good.
GGML_NATIVE=ON lets the compiler target the exact build host ISA; may improve matmul kernels slightly on this CPU (expected small improvement or no_change).
Link-time optimization could inline hot ggml paths; effect on a 135M model is probably within noise (expected no_change).
Forcing --flash-attn on (instead of auto) may change the attention kernel on CPU; check TTFT/FTGR and that greedy outputs stay identical.
Four server slots split the 2048 context; sequential requests should see no gain and possibly a small regression from smaller per-slot KV (expected no_change or regressed).
Skipping the server warmup pass should cut startup-to-first-valid-generation; the primary metrics should be unchanged, so the rule must return no_change (startup is secondary).
Quantizing the K cache to q8_0 shrinks KV memory traffic; it must not change greedy outputs on the benchmark prompts or the golden gate rejects it.
